self.created = True
        try:
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(self.token)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
evidence.reason: The admission marker is treated as a persistent hold: the code fsyncs the token file and has recovery/refusal paths for persistence failures. However, after creating the marker with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and writing/fsyncing the file, it never fsyncs the parent directory, so the directory entry itself can be lost on power failure. That can reboot the host without the intended admission hold. The same durability gap applies when releasing by unlinking. This is an ordinary crash-consistency defect in the existing intended behavior, not a new requirement; the minimal fix is to fsync the parent directory after creation and removal and report failure as an unverified admission transition.
